subject: humanities
passage: Beginning in the sixteenth century, metalworkers in the Kingdom of Benin, in what is now southern Nigeria, cast hundreds of rectangular brass plaques for the royal palace. The ______ which once covered the wooden pillars of the palace, show the oba, or king, along with court officials, warriors, musicians, and European traders. Many of the plaques are now held in museums in Europe and North America.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The clause "which once covered the wooden pillars of the palace" is extra information about the plaques. It closes with a comma before the verb "show," so it must also open with a comma after "plaques."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Extra information must be set off by matching marks; a dash can't open a phrase that closes with a comma.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "The plaques" from the rest of its own clause.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without an opening comma, the comma before "show" would separate the subject from its verb.
explanation.D: Correct. The comma opens the pair of commas around the nonessential "which" clause, matching the comma before "show."
